source_identity_crosscheck.safe_historical_probe: manifest records classifier-only PASS for benign, delete, formatting and nested-shell cases; no destructive command executed
source_identity_crosscheck.boundary: exact archived bytes and a bounded historical classifier probe do not prove current Frankenstein runtime installation or scheduler reachability

semantic_atoms.claim: wache-koenig is a genuine pre-execution blocker for selected Bash commands when installed: non-Bash exits without coverage; classified Bash commands may hard-deny or require a valid command-bound ticket; the hook relies on host scheduler exit semantics for blocking.

The historical grant path binds a ticket to the exact command hash, delayed validity and expiry, then unlinks it on successful consumption; freigabe obtains the grant through a separate controlling TTY. This is a concrete owner-capability-lease precursor, not a sufficient typed EntityOS effect capability.

architecture_deltas.delta: Preserve out-of-model grant separation, scope binding, expiry and one-shot consumption. Replace raw command-text ticket authority with a typed EffectDecision/lease bound to invocation_id/tool_use_id + request_digest + resolved resource identity + generation + causal_id + policy/executor identity.

Do not credit wache-koenig as a complete predecessor EffectGate: its source deliberately ignores non-Bash tools. Triggerword 4 must converge Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/Bash/realtime effects onto one deterministic executor/effect boundary or explicitly prove separate adapters consume the same canonical typed decision.

The source-recovery P0 is closed at byte identity, but runtime lineage remains open. Recover exact global settings/scheduler registration, matcher and ordering before assigning historical or current runtime reachability to this watcher.

contradictions.resolution: Current stern normal admission is nonblocking bookkeeping; historical wache-koenig is genuinely blocking for selected Bash calls when installed. They are distinct authority classes and must not be collapsed under one EffectGate label.

contradictions.resolution_rule: Exact source bytes are recovered, but scheduler/settings binding and current installation are not. Source capability is not runtime reachability.
Bash-only gate cannot establish one complete real-effect authority for other state-changing tool classes.

hypotheses: The strongest Frankenstein-2.0 effect successor fuses three donor invariants: historical human pre-execution denial, historical one-shot out-of-model owner grants, and current stern generation/idempotency/post-outcome journaling, but moves final authority into one executor-consumed typed decision boundary.

A canonical typed effect lease will be safer than raw command-hash tickets because it can bind resolved resources, generation, executor identity and non-shell effects without relying on regex equivalence.
counterhypotheses: A newer host permission layer may already supersede wache-koenig and cover more tools; exact current host configuration should be preferred if recovered.
For shell-only effects a command-hash ticket may remain simpler; migration complexity is justified only if tests demonstrate aliasing/resource/cwd/environment gaps or cross-tool convergence value.
next_exact_gate: Recover the exact historical/current hook scheduler/settings registration and ordering for wache-koenig or its successor, trace non-Bash mutating tools and realtime function calls to their actual execution boundary, then require Triggerword-4 one-shot decision-consumption tests across Bash/Write/Edit plus mismatch/stale/duplicate/deny/unknown-outcome cases.
